name: Jewellery (gold, diamond, artificial)

problems.words: Weight in the register and on the scale don't match at month end
quick_ideas: Do one full weigh-in of every tray against its tags, because it shows whether the gap is in a few trays or spread across the stock
List every piece currently outside the showcase (safe, karigar, exhibition, on approval), because much "missing" weight is simply somewhere else.

workzap_build.text: staff check a tray or two on phone every day by tag and weight, and the owner's morning read shows stock weight by branch with any tray that didn't match.

problems.ask_first: Do you track by piece tag, by total weight, or both?
problems.free_stops: the daily check rotation, tolerance limits and how the register is restructured go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the heaviest trays with their register weights once this week, so you can see where the month-end mismatch clusters.
Give one person the job of noting every piece moved out of the showcase in one notebook, so outside stock stops muddying the count.

problems.words: Gold given to the karigar comes back less and we can't tell why
quick_ideas: Settle the full balance with each karigar once, job by job, because it shows whether the difference sits with certain work or is general
Agree the allowed khot for bridal and other heavy work in writing, because anything above it then stands out.

workzap_build.text: a karigar ledger where every issue and receipt is entered on phone, the running balance updates itself and the owner is alerted the moment a job crosses its allowed khot.

problems.ask_first: Do your karigars work in-house or do you send work outside?
problems.free_stops: how the ledger, approval steps and alert limits are set up is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the weight sent out and weight returned for each karigar job this week, so the mismatch can be tied to specific work.
Make one person responsible for writing every karigar handover in one notebook, so each return can be matched to one outgoing entry.

problems.words: We don't know which custom orders are pending, and the bridal set isn't ready on the promised date
quick_ideas: Write every open order on one list with its promised date and stage, because seeing them together shows which are already at risk
Agree a rule that the workshop finishes ahead of the customer's date, because wedding season needs a buffer.

workzap_build.text: every order tracked from bayana to handover with photo, stage and karigar, a "due this week" list each morning and status updates to customers who agree to them.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many custom orders run at once in peak season?
problems.free_stops: the stages, buffer rules and customer update flow are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many open bridal and custom orders are already past their workshop stage today, so late jobs stand out early.
Give one staff member the job of checking the open-order notebook every afternoon, so promised dates get chased before they slip.

problems.words: Rates change during the day and staff quote yesterday's rate
quick_ideas: Pick one place where the day's rate is announced and make it the only source staff may quote from, because mixed sources cause wrong quotes
Note on each estimate the rate used, because disputes can then be checked.

workzap_build.text: the owner enters the rate once and it reaches tags, billing and every salesperson's phone, time-stamped, across all branches.

problems.ask_first: How does the rate reach the counter today?
problems.free_stops: how the rate flows into billing and tags is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare today's quoted rates across staff once during trading hours, so you can spot whether yesterday's rate is still being used.
Give one person the job of writing the current rate in one visible place each morning, so staff quote from the same source.

problems.words: Making charges are negotiated differently by each salesman
quick_ideas: Go through one month of bills by salesman, because it shows who gives away the most mazdoori
Agree a lowest acceptable making charge per category with your team, because it gives everyone the same starting point.

workzap_build.text: category rules applied at billing, an approval request to the owner below the limit, and a weekly view of discounts by salesperson.

problems.ask_first: Who decides making charges today, you or each salesman?
problems.free_stops: the actual bands, limits and approval routing go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare bills from different salesmen for similar pieces this week, so uneven making charges show up in real transactions.
Give one person the job of keeping one written list of agreed making charges by category, so everyone starts from the same number.

problems.words: Stock went to an exhibition and not everything came back accounted for
quick_ideas: Make a tag-by-tag list of what goes to the next exhibition, because without a list nobody can prove a shortfall
Have two people sign it out and back, because it removes doubt about who checked.

workzap_build.text: tag scan out and in for exhibitions and branch moves, with an instant shortfall list for anything sent but not returned.

problems.ask_first: Do pieces also move between your branches?
problems.free_stops: the checkout and check-in process and its controls are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the exhibition return against the outgoing tag list once, so you can see whether the shortfall is tags, pieces or paperwork.
Give one person the job of holding the single exhibition movement list from packing to return, so nothing changes hands without one record.

problems.words: Booking advances are in a diary and sometimes we can't find them
quick_ideas: Copy every advance currently held onto one list and total it, because you'll know exactly what is owed in goods
Switch to numbered receipts, because a missing number shows a missing entry.

workzap_build.text: every advance and booking balance linked to its order, with total advances held shown in the owner's daily read.

problems.ask_first: Do you also run instalment or booking schemes?
problems.free_stops: how advances link to orders and billing is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many booking advances in the diary have no matching slip or note today, so missing records show up at once.
Give one person the job of keeping all advance entries in one notebook at the counter, so staff stop searching through old diary pages.

problems.words: Instagram DMs ask ‘price?' all day and nobody replies properly
quick_ideas: Count a day's enquiries and how many got a proper reply, because it shows the size of the leak
Give one person ownership of the inbox, because shared inboxes get ignored.

workzap_build.text: one inbox for Instagram and WhatsApp where every enquiry is assigned, answered consistently and followed up on time, with a daily count of missed ones.

problems.free_stops: reply flows, catalogue links and follow-up timings are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many price enquiries arrive in one busy period and how many get a clear reply, so the missed demand becomes visible.
Give one person the job of checking all price enquiries at fixed times daily, so replies stop getting lost in shared chat handling.

problems.words: Repairs and resizing jobs get lost, or a customer's piece goes missing
quick_ideas: List every repair piece in the shop right now against its slip, because it shows which ones have no paper trail
Photograph pieces at intake from today, because it settles condition and identity later.

workzap_build.text: repair cards with intake photo and weight, stage and karigar, and a message when it's ready to customers who agree.

problems.ask_first: Are repairs done in-house or sent out?
problems.free_stops: the intake and handover process is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare every repair and resizing piece in the shop with its slip today, so you can spot which jobs have no matching paper.
Give one person the job of receiving every repair into one notebook before it moves anywhere, so missing pieces can be traced sooner.

problems.words: Salesmen fight over commission, and the top one left with his customers
quick_ideas: Write the commission rule down and share it, because disputes start where the rule is unclear
Move enquiries from salesmen's phones to a shop record, with customers' permission, because the relationship then stays with the shop.

workzap_build.text: sales credited to each person at billing with commission worked out automatically, and a shop-owned customer list (with permission) that stays when staff leave.

problems.ask_first: How is commission worked out today?
problems.free_stops: the commission logic and customer list setup go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note for one week how many walk-ins each salesman starts and how many bills follow, so commission arguments can be checked fairly.
Assign one person to write each new enquiry into one shop notebook before handover, so customer follow-up stays with the shop.

problems.words: I'm scared about cash in the shop at closing
quick_ideas: Agree that closing is never done alone, because two people make it safer and clearer
Move cash out during the day, because less sits in the shop at night; if there's ever a threat, call the police (15 in PK, 999 in the UAE, 911 in Canada).

workzap_build.text: a nightly close per branch matching cash, card, transfer and old-gold value against the day's bills, sent to the owner.

problems.ask_first: Is most payment cash, card, transfer or old-gold exchange?
problems.free_stops: the close-out steps and reporting are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the latest time cash still sits in the shop across one week, so you can see which evenings feel most exposed.
Give one person the closing cash checklist in one notebook at the same time each night, so the handover stays consistent.

never_say: Anything about whether gold is a good buy, where rates are heading, or whether to hold, melt or sell.
Any valuation, grading or authentication of pieces or diamond certificates.
Advice on VAT on gold, anti-money-laundering, hallmarking or dealer registration; say "please check with your accountant or compliance adviser".
Help to under-invoice, split invoices, hide cash sales or buy gold without paperwork.
Any accusation of a karigar or staff member, or a promise that losses will be recovered.

sample_reply.person: Bhai karigar wala masla ka koi hal batao. Har dafa sona kam wapis aata hai, khaas tor pe bridal sets mein.
sample_reply.pi: Ji haan, is ka hal bilkul mumkin hai. 1. Har karigar ka poora hisaab ek dafa job ke hisaab se mila lein, is se pata chalega ke farq kuch khaas kaam mein hai ya har jagah. 2. Bridal sets ke liye khot ki had likh kar tay kar lein, taake us se zyada farq foran nazar aaye. Workzap ye kaam aap ke liye khud-ba-khud kar sakta hai: har job ka sona diya aur wapis aaya phone pe darj ho, balance khud update ho aur had se zyada farq pe aap ko usi waqt alert mile. Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
